title: Why 95% of backtested "edges" die in production (and what actually worked after months of testing)
author: param13131

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
point 2 bit me hardest. on options the spread does most of the damage, a backtest that fills at the midpoint hides a chunk of every round trip. filling option backtests at the bid or the ask instead of the middle is what I made Quantradin for, it's free. quantradin.com

did any of your rules survive once the spread went in?

replies.author: param13131
replies.body: In those cases, I’ve noticed that regime filters often improve performance in specific historical periods but fail to generalize across different market conditions. How can we distinguish genuine, repeatable market edges from overfitted regime filters and identify which strategies are likely to work in the current market regime?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: pick the filter's threshold on one stretch of years, freeze it, then run it on years it never saw. if the edge only lives in the years that set the threshold, it's fit. a real one still works out of sample, just weaker. and if the rule is dead without the filter, the filter is probably rescuing noise.
